continuation.exact_next_action: Design and finitely test a Chat-native repository-only effect-admission protocol in which every effect is immutable and carries owner generation, and acceptance can be validated without a protected shared fence or richer-mode executor. Falsify any design where owner advancement and effect publication are two independent mutable writes that admit a stale generation after a crash. Do not start the separate negative-path acceptance-table leaf in the same invocation.

frozen_authority.note: Earlier pre-refresh semantic scratch was discarded. The bounded slice below was rerun only after matching current root/role reads.

negative_evidence_preserved.meaning: CAS-before-fence is not safe under the tested admission model; this negative result remains part of the frontier.

phase1_acceptance.conflict_check: role-local own-state only; no other-role semantics or shared ledger read; no scheduler mutation
phase1_acceptance.finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota_dependen: none consumed by the finite model; no quota-bearing feature is accepted as part of the route
phase1_acceptance.incremental_monetary_cost: zero for the role-local finite model
phase1_acceptance.reason: The repaired handoff still assumes an authorized cross-role/shared ownership and external effect-fence enforcement surface. This clean role cannot establish that capability from role-local Chat state, so the mechanism remains an unresolved child rather than a Phase-1 pass.
phase1_acceptance.residual_richer_mode_or_protected_or_use: No richer-mode/manual step was executed in this probe, but deployment of the handoff exclusivity property requires a shared effect-admission/fencing capability not available to this role-local surface.

finding.duplicate_delivery_result: replaying offer/fence/CAS is idempotent in the finite model; it does not create a second generation
finding.minimal_counterexample: offer -> owner CAS -> crash before fence: owner is target at g+1 while fence remains g, so a generation-g source effect is still admitted
finding.repair_candidate: Fence first, then ownership CAS. A crash between fence and CAS sacrifices availability but not exclusivity: source still owns g yet cannot externally effect at g, and recovery can roll forward the same CAS.
finding.stale_ack_result: an H1 ack delivered after H2 advances ownership to g+2 is a no-op because ack is bound to exact current target/generation

model.ack_rule: ack is observational only; it never grants ownership or side-effect authority and is valid only while the exact committed target/generation is current
model.duplicate_rule: offer and fence are idempotent; duplicate CAS for the same committed handoff is a no-op; stale generation CAS fails
model.effect_rule: a protected effect carrying generation k is accepted only when k >= current fence generation
revised_protocol: prepare monotone side-effect fence to g+1

slice.question: Can ownership CAS precede external side-effect fencing while preserving stale-owner exclusion under crash/replay?
slice.selection_reason: Exact first continuation from the current role-local Phase-1 architecture checkpoint; narrow causal test of the handoff crash boundary.
